newsitem.title: TAIWAN: No scope for big Taiwan dollar fall - central bank.
newsitem.headline: No scope for big Taiwan dollar fall - central bank.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar's comparison indices against other major foreign currencies had declined since early 1996, giving no room for the local unit to depreciate sharply, the central bank said on Wednesday.

The central bank official told journalists the figures indicated the Taiwan dollar had depreciated considerably against other major currenices with which Taiwan is competitive in exports. The official said this factor had helped improve Taiwan exporters' competitiveness.
"The Taiwan dollar has not been overvalued, and in the future it has no room to fall sharply," the official said.

The indices, including the bilateral trade-weighted index and the export-weighted index, are designed to indicate the currency value and would show the Taiwan dollar was overvalued if the indices were over 100.
In October 1996, the bilateral trade-weighted index fell to 91.2 from 93.67 in January and the export-weighted index was down to 91.5 from 95.36, according to central bank figures.
However, the central bank official said the indices were only one of the factors the central bank used to judge if the Taiwan dollar was at an appropriate level.
The official repeated the central bank's principle of allowing market supply and demand to decide the Taiwan dollar's movement.
The foreign exchange market reacted calmly to the central bank comments in early trading on Wednesday.
After one hour of trade, the Taiwan dollar was at T$27.547 against its American counterpart, compared with Tuesday's T$27.545 close.
